BiblicalUsage: Sephar is a place in Arabia, named in the table of nations as the eastern edge of Joktan's sons' dwelling. Their land stretched from Mesha as far as Sephar, a mount of the east. It is a boundary marker, showing how far the family of Shem had spread.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe even a place named once, on the edge of the map, matters — God watched over the spreading of every family.
